title: `BIGINT << BIGINT`
description: Raises on a negative operand, on bits shifted out, and on shifts below 0 or beyond 63 (but `0 << y` is 0 for any `y`).
The docs are silent on negative operands, shifted-out bits and out-of-range shifts: a docs gap.
reference: `shift_left` drops the bits shifted out, and raises on shifts below 0 or beyond 63.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe` runs the function at each signature on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the 64-bit bounds, 0.5, ±2.5, 1e308, ±inf, NaN, NULL), one row at a time from columns, under every combination of `error_on_division_by_zero` and `ieee_floating_point_ops`. Lean evaluates the Substrait call on the same rows once per candidate value of its option (`substrait-check --outcomes`), and the candidates whose outcomes all match are DuckDB's options. No input is -0.0 (duckdb-R14).

evidence.note: BitwiseShiftLeftOperator: max_shift is the type's bit width; a negative operand, a shift below 0 or at least the width (unless the input is 0), and lost bits raise

provenance.notes: One template for every width, with the range relative to the width: at i8 a shift of 8 or more raises (`0 << 8` is 0), and `1::TINYINT << 7` raises since 128 does not fit. sverify's reference states the range for 64 bits.

evidence.note: for TINYINT, SMALLINT, INT and BIGINT, a statement of `1 << -1`, `1 >> -1`, `1 << w` and `1 >> w` with w past the width (12, 20, 40, 1000) raises
in-range shifts of TINYINT (and SMALLINT, INTEGER, BIGINT below): `1 << 1` → 2, `1 >> 1` → 0

provenance.notes: The error is per statement, so the test does not name the expression that raised; `>>` gives 0 out of range (duckdb-R15-shift-right), so it is `<<`, at i8, i16 and i32 as at i64. `shift_right`'s out-of-range result has no test at these widths.
